name: The incident file excises reporters by recompute
non_visual_rationale: An incident file's whole effect is which stored bytes exist; no user surface is involved. The shipped default is the file absent, which this step proves is byte-identical to today. U1-U8 and a Vera walk are N/A.
criteria_delivered: 1. learned/overrides/v1/reporter-weights.json: a flat map of reporter_key to weight. Absent means every weight is one -- and so does an empty file, and so does an unreadable one, each proven separately.

2. A reporter at weight zero vanishes from the fit byte-identically to their mornings never being stored. Not merely weighted zero: they leave n, the distinct-reporter gate, the physical noise floor's n, the day medians, the concordance record and the propensity numerator, because the excision happens before the observation log reaches any of them.

3. Overrides adjudicate reporters after an incident, never individual reports. A weight between zero and one down-weights the person and leaves every morning of theirs in the fit; no granularity below a reporter exists anywhere in the reader or the writer.
scope_note: TAKEN OUT OF ORDER, DELIBERATELY. The roadmap lists this step's dependency as 04-05, which is escalated and not landed (see 04-05-contract.json). That dependency is a sequencing statement, not a code one: this step needs reporter_key, which landed at 04-03, and a reader plus a multiplier. Nothing here touches the offset estimator or is touched by it, and the byte-identity oracle is independent of it. Landing it leaves the slice at five of six delivered with one open decision, which is worth more than leaving it at four. The roadmap named weights.ts and inputs.ts; residuals.ts was touched only to export the existing reporter_key resolver so fit.ts uses one copy rather than a second, and fit.ts and correction-file.ts were touched because that is where the file has to reach.
design_decisions_not_stated_upstream: WEIGHT ZERO IS AN EXCISION AT THE TOP OF THE RUN, NOT A MULTIPLICATION. 06 section 6.4 gives the file as weights and says nothing about where zero is applied. Criterion 2 settles it: a sample merely multiplied by zero still counts toward n, toward the distinct-reporter gate, toward the n inside the physical noise floor, and still sits in its morning's median where it can move somebody else's fence. So the rows are dropped in fit.ts before the log reaches eligibility, before the spots are counted, before the propensity denominators and before a single residual is formed. Mutation T4 is the proof this placement is load-bearing rather than tidy: excising the same reporter one stage later, after the weighing room, leaves their fingerprint in the stored bytes and the acceptance oracle catches it.

THIS IS THE ONE FILTER IN THIS LANE THAT ALSO REMOVES A SPOT FROM spots_examined, and it breaks with the trust gate's precedent on purpose. 06 section 7 keeps a spot examined even when every one of its reports was ineligible, because the gate excludes SAMPLES from the fit and nothing more. An incident file says something different: those mornings should never have been in the log at all. Byte-identity to 'never stored' is the criterion, and a spot that only the campaign ever reported was, in the world the file describes, never reported.

AN UNREADABLE FILE NAMES NOBODY. 06 section 6.4 does not say what a corrupt incident file means. The one thing this reader must never do is turn a bad byte into somebody being dropped from the fit: erring that way silently removes honest people, while erring the other way leaves the campaign in place with the incident still open and a human still looking. Non-numeric entries and negative weights are ignored for the same reason.

A WEIGHT ABOVE ONE IS ACCEPTED AS WRITTEN rather than clipped. The file is human-edited by pull request and reviewed as a diff; a reviewer who sees 2 in it can see it. Silently clipping would mean the file and the fit disagree about what the file says, which is worse than either reading. Concordance keeps its own ceiling because it is machine-derived and nobody reviews it.
acceptance: tests/acceptance/f-forecast-learns-from-the-beach/an-incident-file-excises-reporters.test.ts, three examples over the real runLearningFitOnce port with the incident file in the same in-memory store. Twenty-two honest mornings from seven reporters, plus one device piling onto the first six of them claiming double overhead and epic, which is what a coordinated push actually looks like. THE ORACLE IS BYTE IDENTITY TWICE OVER: the excised run against a run where the campaign's mornings were never written, and the absent, empty and unreadable files against each other. The first example also asserts up front that the campaign DOES move the stored numbers when nobody excises it, so that the byte-identity claim cannot pass by the campaign having been harmless all along.
unit_law: Two fast-check properties in tests/unit/learning-weight-laws.test.ts against applyOverrideWeights, whose exported signature is its port. (1) A named weight multiplies that reporter's samples and nobody else's, changes no reported VALUE, and drops nothing -- removal is a different act at a different place. (2) An empty file is the identity over a free mixture of samples, which is the shipped default.
test_budget: Behaviours: (1) a reporter at weight zero vanishes byte-identically, (2) an absent, empty or unreadable file changes nothing, (3) a weight between zero and one down-weights without excising. Three behaviours, budget 6. Delivered 5: 3 acceptance examples and 2 unit properties.
red_evidence: The acceptance file was written first and run against the 04-04 body. RED with two semantic AssertionErrors: 'an excised reporter still left 28 mornings in the count against 22: weight zero has to come out of every gated count, not just out of the average', and 'a weight of half stored -0.3717467425296469, the same number full weight stores: the file's weights are being read as a yes-or-no'. The absent-file example passed on arrival, correctly: the shipped default is that no file exists and today's behaviour is the one it pins.
falsifiability_evidence: Four controlled mutations, each planted alone against a byte-snapshot of src/learning, each reverted, the revert verified with diff -r ('REVERT CLEAN'), the suite re-run green. (T1) weight zero applied as a multiplier instead of an excision: caught on the count, 28 mornings against 22. (T2) an unreadable incident file allowed to throw instead of naming nobody: caught by the unreadable-file example. (T3) the file read as a yes-or-no, so any named reporter is excised whatever their weight: caught by the down-weight example. (T4) THE PLACEMENT MUTATION, and the one worth the most: the excision moved downstream of the weighing room so the day medians and the propensity denominators still saw the campaign. The counts all come out right and only the byte-identity oracle catches it -- 'a reporter at weight zero must vanish byte-identically to their mornings never being stored: anything less leaves their fingerprint in n, in the error floor or in a day's median'.
gates_run: npm run typecheck exit 0. Full suite at --maxWorkers=4: 501 tests, 496 passed, up from 04-04's 496 across 95 files, which is exactly this step's 5 new tests; the same 5 failures in the same 4 files this lane does not own. npx astro build exit 0.
